newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU to meet unions, employers on code of conduct.
newsitem.headline: EU to meet unions, employers on code of conduct.

text.p: EU social affairs ministers will meet trade unionists and employers on April 15 in Brussels to discuss a code of conduct for companyies planning plant closures.

The move was prompted by French car giant Renault which shocked workers in late February with an announcement that it would close its profitable Vilvoorde plant in Belgium with the loss of 3,100 jobs.
A spokesman for the Dutch social affairs and employment ministry said on Monday that next week's special meeting had been called as a follow-up to an informal meeting in Rotterdam last month.
The Netherlands currently holds the European Union presidency.
In Rotterdam, ministers from the 15-member bloc called for a clear code of conduct governing business closures, which should ensure a period of consultation and information.
They also suggested governments should strengthen their national laws to avoid a repeat of the Renault scenario.

A statement after the Rotterdam meeting said information and consultation were essential conditions for social acceptance of restructuring, and that the involvement of workers was "most important" in such far-reaching changes.

Vilvoorde's angry Renault workers won moral victories in Belgium and France last week when courts ruled Renault had broken the law on prior consultation with workers and therefore had to restart the closure process from scratch.
However Renault said this did not affect its plan to close the plant.
The April 15 meeting comes just before the next formal social affairs council on April 17 in Luxembourg.
